loader every application shares refuses a key supplied by both the environment and a file,
and a value that lives in a file is one the kubelet can rotate under a running process.

grafanaDashboard.description:
Grafana dashboard delivery, consumed by `common.grafana.dashboard.*`. A consuming chart
exposes this shape wherever it likes — `metrics.dashboard` is the convention — and passes it in
as the `values` argument. Grafana has no Kubernetes-native dashboard type, so the partials
render both mechanisms: a labelled ConfigMap for the sidecar, and, optionally, one
`GrafanaDashboard` per file for grafana-operator v5.

enabled.description:
Create the ConfigMap holding the dashboard JSON. Required by the operator path too, which
references it rather than duplicating the JSON into the custom resources.
enabled.title: enabled

allowCrossNamespaceImport.description:
Let the resources bind to Grafana instances outside the release namespace. With `false`
the operator only considers Grafana custom resources in the same namespace.
allowCrossNamespaceImport.title: allowCrossNamespaceImport

enabled.description:
Also create one `GrafanaDashboard` per dashboard file. This is the only delivery path a
chart can make cross-namespace on its own terms. Requires the `grafana.integreatly.org/v1beta1`
CRDs; `common.grafana.dashboard.errors` fails the render loudly rather than silently
dropping the objects when they are absent.
enabled.title: enabled

folder.description: Folder to file the dashboards under. Empty leaves them at the Grafana root.
folder.title: folder

instanceSelector.description:
Label selector for the Grafana instances to import into. Must select something: unlike a
Kubernetes label selector, an empty `instanceSelector` matches no instance at all.
instanceSelector.title: instanceSelector

resyncPeriod.description:
How often the operator re-reconciles the dashboard, undoing edits made in the Grafana UI.
A Go duration.
resyncPeriod.title: resyncPeriod

label.description:
Label a Grafana sidecar watches for dashboard ConfigMaps. Discovery is a property of the

covers the namespace it lands in, which a chart cannot influence from its own side.

networkPolicy.description:
Network policy configuration.

Every generated egress rule is scoped by a `to:` selector. An egress rule that lists only
ports is not a restriction — the NetworkPolicy API reads a missing `to` as "any
destination", so such a policy permits traffic to every in-cluster service and to the
cloud metadata endpoint.

Baseline for the pod security context. `restricted` applies the Pod Security Standards
restricted profile (`runAsNonRoot`, `seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault`,
`fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch`); `none` applies nothing. Identity fields
(`runAsUser`, `runAsGroup`, `fsGroup`) are always left to the chart, since they must match
the UID baked into the image.
podSecurityContextPreset.title: podSecurityContextPreset

prometheusRule.description:
Prometheus recording and alerting rules, consumed by `common.prometheus.rules.*`. Unlike the
dashboards there is only one carrier — `PrometheusRule` is already the operator's own CRD — and
no per-object cross-namespace grant: which namespaces a Prometheus loads rules from is decided
by `ruleNamespaceSelector` and `ruleSelector` on the Prometheus custom resource.

enabled.description:
Create a PrometheusRule from the chart's rule files. Requires the `monitoring.coreos.com/v1`
CRDs; `common.prometheus.rules.errors` fails the render loudly rather than silently dropping
the object when they are absent.
enabled.title: enabled

labels.description:
Extra labels, templated. This is the only half of rule discovery a chart controls: a
cluster whose Prometheus selects `release: kube-prometheus-stack` needs that label here, or
the rules are created and never loaded.
labels.title: labels

scope.description:
Confine the rules to a subset of the cluster's series. A `PrometheusRule` is not scoped to
the namespace it lives in, so `up{job="api"} == 0` matches somebody else's `api` job in
another namespace and two installs of one chart alert on each other. Rather than parse PromQL
in a Go template, the rule files mark every selector with an always-true placeholder matcher
and the library swaps it for a real one — see the note in `_prometheus.tpl`. Consuming charts
normally derive `matcher` rather than exposing it raw.

matcher.description:
What to swap it for, e.g. `namespace="prod"`. Empty disables the substitution; the
placeholder is left in place, which is correct, because it is already a no-op matcher.
matcher.title: matcher

placeholder.description:
The literal placeholder written into the rule files, e.g. `myapp_scope=~".*"`. Empty
disables the substitution and the files install exactly as vendored.
placeholder.title: placeholder

scope.title: scope

prometheusRule.title: prometheusRule

rolloutOnChange.description:
Add `checksum/*` pod annotations so a configuration change rolls the Deployment. Off by
default, and deliberately so: the proxy watches the directories its configuration came from
and rebuilds its client, path patterns, credentials and listener in place when the kubelet
updates the mounted ConfigMap or Secret, which is strictly better than a rollout. Turn this
on only if you want configuration changes to behave like an ordinary image bump.
`telemetry.*` is installed once per process and needs a restart either way.
rolloutOnChange.title: rolloutOnChange

file name is what the loader parses. Set, the chart renders no Secret of its own and
`cloudflare.clientId` / `cloudflare.clientSecret` are ignored.

paths.description:

`/webhook/.*` matches `/webhook/github` but not `/api/webhook/github`. Methods are `ALL`,
`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`. Required — a proxy with no allowed path
forwards nothing.
Example:
  "/webhook/.*":
    - ALL
  "/api/public/.*":
    - GET
    - POST
